response.text:
I can’t view or inspect images in this chat session, so I cannot directly verify the contents of the warehouse photo or read the safety sign you mention. I won’t guess or claim I saw anything. Here’s what I can do and what I need from you to help:

What I cannot verify now
- Any visual details in the attached image (objects, people, sign text, colors, layout).
- Exact wording on the safety sign or whether the sign is legitimate or altered.
- Identities of any people or private information visible in the photo.

What I can do if you provide more information
- If you re-upload the image (or paste a clear crop of the safety sign) I can transcribe legible text, describe visible hazards and objects (without identifying people), and explain the meaning and recommended safety steps.
- If you copy-and-paste the sign text here, I can interpret it, check regulatory or best-practice relevance, and suggest corrective actions or compliant wording.
- If you describe what you see (brief notes), I can help analyze risk, suggest safety improvements, or provide sample wording for a better sign.

Tips to make visual text transcription and hazard analysis accurate
- Provide a close-up crop of the sign without glare or reflections.
- Use a straight-on photo (avoid heavy angle), good lighting, high resolution.
- Include a photo of the surrounding area so I can describe contextual hazards (forklifts, stacked pallets, exposed wiring).
- If there are multiple signs, crop each separately or number them and provide photos or transcribed text.

Examples of common warehouse safety sign text (for reference only)
- “Hard Hats Required Beyond This Point”
- “High Voltage — Authorized Personnel Only”
- “Caution: Forklift Traffic”
- “Emergency Exit — Keep Clear”
- “Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Required: Safety Glasses, Steel-Toe Boots”
These are only examples — I’m not saying your sign says any of these.

Next step
- Reattach the image (a clear crop of the sign) or paste the sign text here, and I’ll transcribe and analyze it, or
- Tell me how you’d like me to help (e.g., interpret sign wording, suggest compliant wording, evaluate hazards).
